newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo govt outlines 1997 economic priorities - media.
newsitem.headline: Yugo govt outlines 1997 economic priorities - media.

text.p: The Yugoslav government has identified currency and price stability as its key 1997 economic priorities, Belgrade media reported on Wednesday.
"The government is firmly committed to strong development of an open and export-driven economy," Politika quoted a Yugoslav Information Ministry statement as saying.

According to the statement, the 1997 economic policy should aim at maintaining currency and price stability, revitalising production and raising standards of living. The government also plans to intensify structural changes and privatisation.
Lack of working capital and hard currency would remain a major barrier hindering faster revival and development of the country's economy.
The 1997 strategy is based on the assumption that Yugoslavia would receive considerably better treatment in the international community and return to world financial and commodities markets.
Yugoslav deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic was named chief coordinator for preparing the final 1997 economic policy paper. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
